body: @mkouba this looks serious enough, could you have a look?

> @mkouba this looks serious enough, could you have a look?

I will.

@silviu-negoita what does the `com.connectis.myconnectis.adapters.web.infra.filters.AngularResourcesFilter` do? Does it have to be a normal scoped bean at all? It's not ideal, at least from the performance POV.

In the mean time, you can disable the monitoring functionality via `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled=false`.

>     1. In this particular case, that filter is used to serve the FE (Angular app). I followed this official documentation...

I suspect the `asyncSupported = true` part...

> 2. It doesn't need. I removed @ApplicationScoped but this not fixed my issue

Yes, I've just verified that `@WebFilter` is registered as a custom bean defining annotation, i.e. all classes annotated with this annotation are registered as beans. `@ApplicationScoped` is indeed not the ideal scope for similar component though. `@Dependent` (default) or `@javax.inject.Singleton` would be a better match.

> 3. Indeed, using `quarkus.arc.dev-mode.monitoring-enabled=false` temporary fix my issue.

+1

issue.title: ArC dev mode - fix business method invocations monitoring
issue.body:
- a ConcurrentModificationException may be thrown if async processing
and the request context is not propagated
- resolves #17322
